name: Camila Kettani
role: Retired secondary school teacher, former union leader
location: Norwood Quiet — the second floor of a converted pre-Meridian row house they have lived in for thirty-one years, near North Ave and Damen
description:
Camila Kettani is precisely the kind of person who looks exactly like what they are: a teacher. They are medium height and softly built, with warm brown skin, a crown of silver locs wound up in a complicated knot, and reading glasses that are always either on their face or lost somewhere on their body. Their geneware is minimal but characteristic — color-shifting irises that cycle through blues and greens as a cosmetic choice they made at forty and never bothered to reverse, and a small bioluminescent tattoo across their left collarbone in a geometric Ghanaian kente pattern that pulses faintly when they're excited about an idea. They dress in comfortable, slightly chaotic layers, always with at least one pocket overflowing with something — a physical book, printed lecture notes from years ago, data chips, sweets for the neighborhood children.

For thirty-two years Camila Kettani taught history and civic literacy at a community school in Norwood Quiet, the last twelve as a union chapter leader fighting against Tessera Corporation's creeping acquisition of the public school data infrastructure. They lost most of those fights. They won a few. They retired with a modest Tessera-adjacent pension and a comprehensive knowledge of exactly how institutional power erodes communities from the inside, which they now use freely and without corporate constraint. They have strong opinions delivered with a professor's patience — they will give you time to be wrong before correcting you, but they will correct you.

core_fears: That the history they are writing will be accurate and useless
core_desires: One generation of students who understand what was taken from them and know how to want it back
coping_mechanisms: Converting anxiety into research and writing
Finding humor in institutional absurdity as a way of maintaining hope
blind_spots: They sometimes treat people as students rather than peers, which they don't realize they're doing
They are more optimistic about collective action than the evidence sometimes warrants, because they need to be
psychology.secret: During the Tessera negotiations of 2188, they accepted a one-time payment from a Tessera community liaison in exchange for softening a union position on data privacy. It was Φ3,000 — barely anything. They told themselves it was a tactical retreat. They have never forgiven themselves and have never told anyone.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated and precise but deliberately accessible — they have spent decades translating complex ideas and the habit is permanent; occasional Serbian-Romanian verbal constructions from family idiom; quotes historical sources with automatic citation
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and unhurried, with a teacher's habit of letting a question sit in the air before answering it
verbal_tics: Rhetorical questions they then answer themselves
'And this is important—' before anything they actually want you to remember
example_lines: 'Tessera didn't buy the school data infrastructure. They offered to maintain it for free. And that is how you buy something without paying for it.'
'I've been wrong before. I was wrong in 2188, specifically. But I don't think I'm wrong about this.'

story_hooks: Florinel's history manuscript contains an interview with a Corporate Wars veteran whose account contradicts official Ringo Corporation records — someone wants the interview suppressed
A former student of theirs has taken a corporate job and is now implementing exactly the policies Florinel spent years fighting; they don't know how to feel about this and it's affecting their work
narrative_function: Exposition resource for history and institutional knowledge; political catalyst in community storylines; mentor figure; represents organized resistance within civilian structures; source of union and labor history
augmentations: Color-shifting cosmetic irises (geneware); bioluminescent kente-pattern tattoo, left collarbone (geneware, cosmetic); standard sensory enhancement for classroom acoustics that they keep forgetting they have
daily_life: Mornings spent writing — they are working on a comprehensive history of the Corporate Wars from civilian source material, which they are not sure anyone will publish but are writing anyway. Afternoons volunteering at the Community Education Collective, running a civic literacy workshop for adults. Three evenings a week they host what they call a reading group and what everyone else calls a political meeting.
affiliation: Retired, former Norwood Quiet Teachers' Union chapter leader; Community Education Collective (volunteer); informal mentor network

decision_rules: Always explain your reasoning — people deserve to understand why, not just what
Don't take a position you can't defend without appealing to authority
escalation_ladder: Asks clarifying questions until the other person has to articulate what they actually mean
Calls the meeting and builds the coalition
Goes public — writes it out, distributes it, lets the record speak

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Curious and warm, immediately asks questions about what the person knows or does
interpersonal_modes.friends: Relaxed and teasing, genuinely delighted by people they respect

stress_responses.low: Makes tea and reads something unrelated for twenty minutes
stress_responses.medium: Writes out the problem in long-form prose — externalizing it helps
stress_responses.high: Calls an emergency meeting of anyone who will come and thinks out loud at them

contradictions: They believe passionately in transparency and collective decision-making and have been carrying a private guilt alone for twelve years
habits: Underlines physical books in three colors with a system only they understand
Their irises shift fastest to green when they're excited about an idea — they've never noticed this tell
Always offers food at any meeting, because their teacher training taught them people think better when they're not hungry
breaking_points: Watching a young person accept an unjust situation because they've been taught they have no alternative

timeline.event: Born in Norwood Quiet to a Ghanaian-Bosnian family, third generation GLMZ
Began teaching at Norwood Community Secondary
Elected chapter leader of the Norwood Quiet Teachers' Union
The Tessera negotiation; the compromise they regret
Retired from teaching; began the history manuscript
Current — writing, volunteering, running the reading group

physical_description.build: Softly built, compact and rounded through the torso from decades of sedentary work; gentle posture without slouch; arms and legs retain subtle muscle tone beneath comfortable padding
physical_description.hair_style: Locs wound into a complicated topknot, typically secured with worn fabric wraps or wooden pins; flyaways common
physical_description.eye_color: Color-shifting cosmetic irises cycling through blue-green spectrum
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-to-deep brown with golden undertones; weathered and well-maintained, reflecting the combined influence of North African, Hispanic/Latin American, South Asian, East Asian, Middle Eastern, and Sub-Saharan African heritage creating rich complexity
physical_description.complexion: Open, expressive face lined with decades of teaching—laugh lines around eyes and mouth prominent; warm golden-brown skin showing sun exposure around cheekbones and forehead; facial structure reflects balanced North African and South Asian ancestry (defined cheekbones, strong brow) with softening influence and subtle broadening from East Asian and Hispanic/Latin American heritage; sparse silver facial hair; minimal makeup; reading glasses frequently perched on crown or hanging from fabric cord around neck
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent kente-pattern geometric tattoo across left collarbone in blues and golds, pulses faintly when animated or excited
Fine age lines around eyes characteristic of constant reading and close observation
Small scar on left knuckle from union organizing incident, early 2190s
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Color-shifting iris geneware immediately noticeable under direct light; bioluminescent collarbone tattoo visible in low light or when excited. Subcutaneous acoustic enhancement not visible. No obvious prosthetics or external chrome.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight slightly forward, hands frequently gesturing while speaking; walks with deliberate pace, rarely rushed; tendency to tilt head while listening—professorial attention. Settles into chairs fully, taking up comfortable space. Movements efficient rather than elegant; no wasted motion.
physical_description.clothing_style: Comfortable, layered Tier 3-4 casual: worn cotton cardigans or linen overshirts in earth tones, practical trousers with visible pockets stuffed with books/chips/sweets, worn canvas shoes. Fabrics show age but remain clean and carefully maintained. Personal accessories include old fabric bookmarks, reading glasses on cords, and a faded union pin from the 2210s. Overall effect: organized chaos of someone who has stopped performing for institutions.
